messages:
liz (eng-runtime): Heads up — repro from perf lab shows a consistent ~18% token throughput drop when using replay harness vs synthetic load. Kernel selector picks a different GEMM path on H100 image, guessing it's an env mismatch (drivers/CUDA/container args).
omar (mlperf): ugh. can you paste the exact envs + image tags? small diffs blow up perf.
liz (eng-runtime): repro steps: use replay harness: `./run_replay.sh --trace=2026-03-10.session --concurrency=24 --capture-kv` on image `registry.redwood-inference/runtime:bench-2026-03-01`. Host A100 test used driver 535.54 / CUDA 12.1; H100 node was on 530.30 / CUDA 11.8. Also the H100 container had `--privileged` removed and `--shm-size=1g`.
rahul (infra): that driver/CUDA mismatch is immediate red flag. kernel selection (cuBLAS heuristics, tuned kernels) can differ across CUDA minor versions. we should standardize to driver 535.x + CUDA 12.1 for the matrix until we validate otherwise.
sophie (perf): also saw KV cache warmup variance. Replay begins with long prefixes so prefix caching changes the effective sequence-length distribution vs synthetic (which used constant seq=512). Need to align the workload distribution for apples-to-apples.
liz (eng-runtime): agree. proposal:
1) Pin driver & CUDA on test nodes: 535.86 + CUDA 12.1 runtime image (image tag `bench-cuda12.1-535.86`).
2) Use a single base container and only swap model artifacts. base: `registry.../runtime:bench-base-cuda12.1-2026-03-01` (includes nsys 2024.4, nvcc toolchain).
3) Add a mandatory KV warmup phase to replay harness: `--kv-warmup=100` (100 BPE prefills) so caches match steady-state.
4) Record exact `nvidia-smi -q` and `dmesg | tail -n 200` and mount `/var/log` for later analysis.
5) Capture profiler snapshots (nsys) for both synthetic and replay runs with same random seed / prompt set.

shell snippet to run (bench template):
```
# on test node
docker run --rm --gpus=all --privileged --shm-size=16g \
  -v /var/log:/host-logs \
  -e CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 \
  registry.redwood-inference/runtime:bench-base-cuda12.1-2026-03-01 \
  /bin/bash -c "nsys profile -o /host-logs/profile.rp --stats=true ./run_replay.sh --trace=... --kv-warmup=100 --concurrency=24"
```
omar (mlperf): Add `TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=garbage_collection_threshold:0.6`? we saw allocator flags change fragmentation and can flip a kernel path.
rahul (infra): good call — but keep alloc flags in a documented matrix. propose env matrix doc: `drivers: [535.86, 530.30]`, `cuda: [12.1, 11.8]`, `images: [bench-base-cuda12.1, bench-base-cuda11.8]`, `kernel-flags: [transparent_hugepage=never, vm.swappiness=10]`.
sophie (perf): Also capture perf counters: `nvidia-smi dmon` and `nsys` timelines. We should compare `sm_efficiency`, `gld_throughput`, and `l2_cache_hit_rate` between runs — those correlate with different GEMM kernels.
liz (eng-runtime): action items:
- rahul: provision 2 nodes (A100/H100) with driver 535.86 + CUDA 12.1 image by EOD tomorrow.
- omar: update replay harness to add `--kv-warmup` + fixed seq distribution and a synthetic trace generator that samples the same prefix length distribution.
- sophie: prepare nsys perf plan and provide the list of counters we'll extract.
- me: run 3 paired runs (synthetic vs replay) on both nodes, collect logs and upload to `/shared/perf/2026-03-11/env-parity/`.

rahul (infra): I'll spin them up and log driver install steps. note: we need kernel flag toggle script to flip THP and vm.swappiness and record values before/after.
omar (mlperf): I'll add the sequence distribution sampler to the harness. will also add a flag `--force-kernel-selector=bfloat16_fallback` for stress tests.
ci-bot: build finished: registry.redwood-inference/runtime:bench-base-cuda12.1-2026-03-01 (sha256:abc123) :white_check_mark:
deploy-bot: new infra nodes scheduled for provisioning (ticket INF-2387).
liz (eng-runtime): great — let's reconvene after the first paired runs. if we still see >8% divergence, escalate to kernel devs and dump cuBLAS logs. :hourglass:
